items.headline: U.S. economy grows at 3.4% pace in third quarter
items.summary: Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, driven by consumer spending and business investment tied to artificial intelligence. It was the last major economic report before the Nov. 3 midterms, though many Americans still say affordability is a struggle.

items.headline: Alaska governor orders probe of Peltola campaign
items.summary: Gov. Mike Dunleavy ordered an investigation into Democrat Mary Peltola's Senate campaign after reports that it helped recruit a second candidate named Dan Sullivan. The allegations have upended one of the races that could decide control of the Senate.

items.headline: Justice Department subpoenas Los Angeles election workers
items.summary: Grand jury subpoenas were sent to election workers in Los Angeles. The move escalates the Trump administration's clash with California officials over voter rolls days before the election.

items.headline: Trump's approval near historic low before midterms
items.summary: TIME reports that President Trump's approval rating is historically low for a president this close to a midterm election. The numbers come as Republicans defend their House and Senate majorities.

items.headline: U.S. and Japan to build joint missile plant in Japan
items.summary: The two allies agreed to set up a facility in Japan for joint missile production. The step comes amid concern over China's growing assertiveness in Asia.

items.headline: China elevates a general to the Politburo
items.summary: China's Communist Party promoted a military general to the Politburo and called for stronger party discipline. The moves come about a year before Xi Jinping is expected to secure a fourth term.

items.headline: Europe rallies around the International Criminal Court
items.summary: European governments are lining up behind the International Criminal Court in defiance of the Trump administration. TIME examines how the split is playing out.

items.headline: Patrick Stewart dies at 86
items.summary: Patrick Stewart, the British actor known for 'Star Trek: The Next Generation' and the 'X-Men' films, has died at 86. He was celebrated for playing paternal leaders of ensembles of misfits.

items.headline: Halloween candy prices up 7.7% in a year
items.summary: Prices for candy and gum have risen 7.7% over the past year and more than 18% over two years, federal data show. Shoppers face higher costs heading into Halloween.

items.headline: Study finds seabirds get jet lag
items.summary: Research on Manx shearwaters suggests the seabirds become disoriented on flights back to their nests because of shifting time zones. NPR reported the findings Thursday.

digest.overview:
The economy grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter on consumer spending and AI investment, the last major report before Tuesday's midterms. Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy ordered an investigation into Democrat Mary Peltola's Senate campaign over reports it helped recruit a second Dan Sullivan, which Peltola denies. The Justice Department subpoenaed Los Angeles election workers as its voter-roll fight with California escalated. The Pentagon told Congress the Iran war has cost at least $47 billion. Democrats lead the generic-ballot average 51.4% to 43.2%, and President Trump's approval is historically low for this point before a midterm. Hackers claimed to leak data on more than 40,000 DHS employees. Actor Patrick Stewart died at 86.

Abroad, Iran's Revolutionary Guard said four vessels caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, while U.S. Central Command said it had cleared the strait. A Russian drone strike on Dnipro's main rail station killed at least 13 people, and Moscow said it downed most of 613 drones aimed at the capital. Netanyahu's Likud amplified unproven claims that Arab-led parties stole Israel's election as final results left his bloc short of a majority. An Israeli strike on a ministry building in Gaza's al-Mawasi killed four. Spain's train-crash death toll rose to 69. The U.S. and Japan agreed to build a joint missile plant in Japan, and China promoted a general to the Politburo. South Korea is weighing a noncombat role in securing Hormuz, such as a patrol aircraft. Venezuela's María Corina Machado called for new elections.

home.overview:
Green Bay opened Week 8 by beating Carolina 27–19 on Thursday night behind three touchdowns from Jordan Love, while Tennessee shipped All-Pro Jeffery Simmons to Chicago and Lamar Jackson is expected back for Baltimore's Sunday trip to Buffalo. In the NBA, Onyeka Okongwu's 29 and 12 lifted Atlanta past Cleveland 114–111, rookie Cameron Boozer recorded his first triple-double as Memphis won 124–103 in Portland, and New Orleans beat Sacramento 132–120. Friday's 10-game slate features Knicks at 76ers and Lakers at Warriors. Milwaukee, with William Contreras named World Series MVP, parades its first title through downtown today.

Everton beat Newcastle 3–1 to reach the Carabao Cup quarterfinals, where they visit Arsenal-conquerors Fleetwood. European weekends start tonight with PSG at Le Havre and Lens at Lille, before Saturday's Der Klassiker in Munich and Chelsea vs. Man United in the Premier League. K League 1's split round begins with Jeonbuk hosting Daejeon in the race for third, and K League 2 leaders Suwon Samsung visit Daegu. In the KBO, Samsung beat Kia 6–4 in Gwangju to lead their playoff 2–1 and can clinch a Korean Series date with KT Wiz in tonight's Game 4.

brief: Samsung beat Kia 6–4 in Gwangju on Thursday to take a 2–1 lead in the best-of-five second round.
Park Seung-gyu broke a 4–4 tie with a two-out RBI double in the seventh, and Koo Ja-wook added an insurance run.
Lewin Diaz and Ryu Ji-hyeok homered for Samsung, while Kim Do-yeong and Na Sung-bum went deep for Kia.
Kia used nine pitchers, tying the postseason record for one team in a game.
Game 4 is Friday in Gwangju; Samsung can clinch a Korean Series date with KT Wiz, which begins Nov. 2.
